- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes, model often overshoots and fails to correct — apply downward bias of 2–5% in subsequent periods.
- If sentiment turns bearish (≤0.33) and news volume drops, model overreacts; adjust forecast downward by 1–4% to align with mean reversion.
- When sentiment change is negative and news volume remains high, model underestimates — increase forecast by 1–3% to capture momentum.
- If model forecast is >10% above true outcome and sentiment is neutral or slightly bullish, apply “mean reversion” correction: subtract 1–2% from forecast for next 3–5 periods.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome is consistently below model, check sentiment history for recent negative sentiment shifts — adjust downward by 1–3% to reflect sentiment decay.
- If sentiment change is positive and news volume is low, model underestimates — increase forecast by 1–2% to capture potential momentum.
- Avoid forecasting when sentiment change is erratic (±0.67+ in 2 consecutive days) — use 3-period moving average to smooth out noise.
